title: The Sunday Space Journal
coverageNote: Original short editorial summaries for 19–25 October 2026. Each report keeps its source and publication date; open the source for the full article.

stories.title: One year inside a Mars-mission simulation
stories.summary: Four volunteers completed a year inside a NASA analog habitat designed to study isolation, routines, and teamwork for a future Mars mission. The exercise is not a trip to Mars; it helps researchers examine human factors and operating challenges during long-duration exploration.

stories.title: Understanding the shake and flex of launch
stories.summary: Rockets experience intense vibration and structural loads on the way to orbit. NASA Kennedy engineers are refining analysis methods to better understand those conditions, helping teams assess how spacecraft structures and sensitive instruments respond before flight.

stories.title: Curiosity watches the clouds over Mars
stories.summary: A new Curiosity rover planning update covers sols 5036–5042 and observations of clouds in the Martian sky. Monitoring clouds helps scientists follow atmospheric conditions and seasonal patterns while the rover continues its work on the surface.

stories.title: Falcon 9 completes the Starlink 15-15 launch
stories.summary: Spaceflight Now reported that a Falcon 9 carried 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base on October 23 after several postponed attempts. The mission highlights the role of California's west-coast launch range in commercial satellite deployment.

stories.title: Artemis III is planned as a systems test in Earth orbit
stories.summary: NASA's October 23 update describes Artemis III as a planned 2027 Earth-orbit mission in which Orion and commercial lander test vehicles would practise rendezvous, docking, and coordinated operations. The aim is to learn how the systems work together before later crewed lunar-surface missions.
